review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

12:1.sourceText: Καὶ ἤρξατο αὐτοῖς ἐν παραβολαῖς λαλεῖν. ἀμπελῶνα ἄνθρωπος ἐφύτευσεν, καὶ περιέθηκεν φραγμὸν καὶ ὤρυξεν ὑπολήνιον καὶ ᾠκοδόμησεν πύργον, καὶ ἐξέδετο αὐτὸν γεωργοῖς, καὶ ἀπεδήμησεν.
12:1.targetText: Then Jesus began to speak to them in parables: “A man planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it, dug a wine vat, and built a watchtower. Then he rented it out to some tenants and went away on a journey.

groups.note: περιέθηκεν "put around" supplies around.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.
BSB uses a comma list here instead of rendering καί.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending of ἤρξατο.
English supplies an object for put around; the Greek has none here.

12:2.sourceText: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς τοὺς γεωργοὺς τῷ καιρῷ δοῦλον, ἵνα παρὰ τῶν γεωργῶν λάβῃ ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος·
12:2.targetText: At harvest time, he sent a servant to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit of the vineyard.

groups.note: τῷ καιρῷ, "at the season", is the season of harvest.
The partitive ἀπό, "(some) from", is rendered share of.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB opens with the time phrase and leaves the connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves παρὰ τῶν γεωργῶν ("from the tenants") unexpressed after collect.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the possessive; the Greek says "from the fruits".

12:3.sourceText: καὶ λαβόντες αὐτὸν ἔδειραν καὶ ἀπέστειλαν κενόν.
12:3.targetText: But they seized the servant, beat him, and sent him away empty-handed.

groups.note: The one object αὐτόν serves all three verbs; BSB names the servant first and repeats him.

12:4.sourceText: καὶ πάλιν ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἄλλον δοῦλον· κἀκεῖνον ἐκεφαλίωσαν καὶ ἠτίμασαν.
12:4.targetText: Then he sent them another servant, and they struck him over the head and treated him shamefully.

groups.note: πρὸς αὐτούς, "to them", is rendered as the indirect object them.
κἀκεῖνον, "and that one", is the object of both verbs; BSB repeats him.
κεφαλιόω means to strike on the head.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves πάλιν ("again") unexpressed; another already marks the next sending.

12:5.sourceText: καὶ ἄλλον ἀπέστειλεν· κἀκεῖνον ἀπέκτειναν, καὶ πολλοὺς ἄλλους, οὓς μὲν δέροντες, οὓς δὲ ἀποκτέννοντες.
12:5.targetText: He sent still another, and this one they killed.  He sent many others; some they beat and others they killed.

groups.note: The one ἀπέστειλεν also governs πολλοὺς ἄλλους; BSB repeats He sent.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.
BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.
The distributive particle μέν is carried by the some ... others contrast without a separate English word.

12:6.sourceText: ἔτι ἕνα εἶχεν, υἱὸν ἀγαπητόν· ἀπέστειλεν αὐτὸν ἔσχατον πρὸς αὐτοὺς λέγων ὅτι Ἐντραπήσονται τὸν υἱόν μου.
12:6.targetText: Finally, having one beloved son, he sent him to them. ‘They will respect my son,’ he said.

groups.note: ἔσχατον, "last", is rendered Finally.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves ἔτι ("still") unexpressed.
ὅτι introduces the direct quotation and has no English counterpart.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:7.sourceText: ἐκεῖνοι δὲ οἱ γεωργοὶ πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς εἶπαν ὅτι Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ κληρονόμος· δεῦτε ἀποκτείνωμεν αὐτόν, καὶ ἡμῶν ἔσται ἡ κληρονομία.
12:7.targetText: But the tenants said to one another, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the demonstrative ἐκεῖνοι ("those") unexpressed; the tenants renders οἱ γεωργοί.
ὅτι introduces the direct quotation and has no English counterpart.

12:8.sourceText: καὶ λαβόντες ἀπέκτειναν αὐτόν, καὶ ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν ἔξω τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος.
12:8.targetText: So they seized the son, killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.

groups.note: The one object αὐτόν serves both seized and killed; BSB names the son first and repeats him.

12:9.sourceText: τί ποιήσει ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος; ἐλεύσεται καὶ ἀπολέσει τοὺς γεωργούς, καὶ δώσει τὸν ἀμπελῶνα ἄλλοις.
12:9.targetText: What then will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and kill those tenants, and will give the vineyard to others.

groups.note: The article τούς points back to the tenants of the parable.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with οὖν ("then") after τί, which N1904 lacks.

12:10.sourceText: οὐδὲ τὴν γραφὴν ταύτην ἀνέγνωτε Λίθον ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες, οὗτος ἐγενήθη εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας·
12:10.targetText: Have you never read this Scripture:  ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.

groups.note: οὐδέ, "not even", is rendered never.
κεφαλὴν γωνίας, "head of the corner", is rendered the cornerstone.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the relative pronoun ὅν (which) unexpressed: "The stone the builders rejected".
The resumptive οὗτος (this one) is not repeated in English after The stone.
The predicate εἰς ("became into") has no separate English word after has become.

12:11.sourceText: παρὰ Κυρίου ἐγένετο αὕτη, καὶ ἔστιν θαυμαστὴ ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς ἡμῶν;
12:11.targetText: This is from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’?”

12:12.sourceText: Καὶ ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν κρατῆσαι, καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν τὸν ὄχλον· ἔγνωσαν γὰρ ὅτι πρὸς αὐτοὺς τὴν παραβολὴν εἶπεν. καὶ ἀφέντες αὐτὸν ἀπῆλθον.
12:12.targetText: At this, the leaders sought to arrest Jesus, for they knew that He had spoken this parable against them. But fearing the crowd, they left Him and went away.

groups.note: The καί joining "sought" and "feared" is rendered as the contrast But.
The article τήν points to the parable just told, rendered this.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB joins this clause to the fearing clause and leaves καί unexpressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending of ἐζήτουν.
English coordinator; the participle ἀφέντες is rendered as the finite verb left.

12:13.sourceText: Καὶ ἀποστέλλουσιν πρὸς αὐτόν τινας τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ τῶν Ἡρῳδιανῶν ἵνα αὐτὸν ἀγρεύσωσιν λόγῳ.
12:13.targetText: Later, they sent some of the Pharisees and Herodians to catch Jesus in His words.

groups.note: The opening καί is rendered as the transition Later.
The dative λόγῳ, "by a word", is rendered in ... words.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves πρὸς αὐτόν ("to Him") unexpressed; the purpose clause names Jesus.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the possessive; the Greek has λόγῳ ("by a word") alone.

12:14.sourceText: καὶ ἐλθόντες λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Διδάσκαλε, οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀληθὴς εἶ καὶ οὐ μέλει σοι περὶ οὐδενός· οὐ γὰρ βλέπεις εἰς πρόσωπον ἀνθρώπων, ἀλλ’ ἐπ’ ἀληθείας τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ διδάσκεις· ἔξεστιν δοῦναι κῆνσον Καίσαρι ἢ οὔ; δῶμεν ἢ μὴ δῶμεν;
12:14.targetText: “Teacher,” they said, “we know that You are honest and seek favor from no one. Indeed, You are impartial and teach the way of God in accordance with the truth. Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar or not? Should we pay them or not?”

groups.note: οὐ μέλει σοι περὶ οὐδενός, "you care about no one", is rendered seek favor from no one.
The Greek double negative οὐ … οὐδενός makes a single English negative.
οὐ βλέπεις εἰς πρόσωπον ἀνθρώπων, "you do not look at the face of men", is rendered You are impartial.
μὴ δῶμεν, "should we not pay", is shortened to not.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καὶ ἐλθόντες ("and coming") unexpressed.
BSB leaves the addressee αὐτῷ ("to Him") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for pay; the Greek δῶμεν has none.

12:15.targetText: But Jesus saw through their hypocrisy and said, “Why are you testing Me? Bring Me a denarius to inspect.”

groups.note: In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun he; BSB names Jesus.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:16.targetText: So they brought it, and He asked them, “Whose image is this? And whose inscription?”  “Caesar’s,” they answered.

12:18.sourceText: Καὶ ἔρχονται Σαδδουκαῖοι πρὸς αὐτόν, οἵτινες λέγουσιν ἀνάστασιν μὴ εἶναι, καὶ ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν λέγοντες
12:18.targetText: Then the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to Jesus and questioned Him:

unmappedSource.reason: The participle λέγοντες ("saying") only introduces the quotation.

12:19.sourceText: Διδάσκαλε, Μωϋσῆς ἔγραψεν ἡμῖν ὅτι ἐάν τινος ἀδελφὸς ἀποθάνῃ καὶ καταλίπῃ γυναῖκα καὶ μὴ ἀφῇ τέκνον, ἵνα λάβῃ ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ τὴν γυναῖκα καὶ ἐξαναστήσῃ σπέρμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ.
12:19.targetText: “Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if a man’s brother dies and leaves a wife but no children, the man is to marry his brother’s widow and raise up offspring for him.

groups.note: μὴ ἀφῇ τέκνον, "does not leave a child", is shortened to but no children, with leaves understood.
ἵνα with the subjunctive λάβῃ ("should take") states the duty, rendered is to marry.
ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ, "his brother", is rendered the man; BSB moves the relationship into his brother's widow.
τὴν γυναῖκα, "the wife" already mentioned, is rendered his brother's widow, spelling out whose wife she was.
τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ, "for his brother", is rendered for him.

12:20.sourceText: ἑπτὰ ἀδελφοὶ ἦσαν· καὶ ὁ πρῶτος ἔλαβεν γυναῖκα, καὶ ἀποθνῄσκων οὐκ ἀφῆκεν σπέρμα·
12:20.targetText: Now there were seven brothers. The first one married and died, leaving no children.

groups.note: ἔλαβεν γυναῖκα, "took a wife", is rendered married.

unmappedSource.reason: The καί is not expressed; BSB starts a new sentence.

12:21.sourceText: καὶ ὁ δεύτερος ἔλαβεν αὐτήν, καὶ ἀπέθανεν μὴ καταλιπὼν σπέρμα· καὶ ὁ τρίτος ὡσαύτως·
12:21.targetText: Then the second one married the widow, but he also died and left no children. And the third did likewise.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds one after the ordinal second.
English adds also, comparing the second brother with the first.

12:22.sourceText: καὶ οἱ ἑπτὰ οὐκ ἀφῆκαν σπέρμα. ἔσχατον πάντων καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἀπέθανεν.
12:22.targetText: In this way, none of the seven left any children. And last of all, the woman died.

groups.note: The opening καί is rendered as the summarizing transition In this way.
The negative οὐκ with the subject οἱ ἑπτά, "the seven did not leave", is rendered none of the seven.
The καί ("also") before ἡ γυνή is rendered as the opening And.

12:23.sourceText: ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει, ὅταν ἀναστῶσιν, τίνος αὐτῶν ἔσται γυνή; οἱ γὰρ ἑπτὰ ἔσχον αὐτὴν γυναῖκα.
12:23.targetText: In the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be? For all seven were married to her.”

groups.note: οἱ ἑπτά, "the seven", is rendered all seven.
ἔσχον … γυναῖκα, "had as wife", is rendered were married.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not separately render ὅταν ἀναστῶσιν ("when they rise"), which restates In the resurrection.
BSB leaves αὐτῶν ("of them") unexpressed after whose.

12:24.sourceText: ἔφη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Οὐ διὰ τοῦτο πλανᾶσθε μὴ εἰδότες τὰς γραφὰς μηδὲ τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ Θεοῦ;

groups.note: Οὐ … πλανᾶσθε, "are you not mistaken", is rendered Aren't you mistaken.
διὰ τοῦτο, "for this reason", points forward to the participle and is rendered because.

12:28.sourceText: Καὶ προσελθὼν εἷς τῶν γραμματέων, ἀκούσας αὐτῶν συνζητούντων, εἰδὼς ὅτι καλῶς ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς, ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτόν Ποία ἐστὶν ἐντολὴ πρώτη πάντων;
